# Content index (English, generated by tools/content_index.py)

Tracks: A = ages 5-8, B = 9-12, C = 13-15, D = 16-17, E = 18+. `l` lesson, `f` FAQ, `m` myth card, `s` scenario.

## d01 — Understanding the Human Body  (allowed tracks: A,B,C,D,E)

Lessons:
- d01-l01 [A] My Body, Real Names — Every body part has a proper name
    sections: Your body is amazing | Private parts have real names too | Private means private | If something feels wrong, tell
    myth addressed: Words like penis and vulva are bad words.
- d01-l02 [B] Outside and Inside: The Body Map — Reproductive organs and the pee route, correctly labelled
    sections: External and internal: two sets of parts | Penis, scrotum and testes | Vulva, vagina, uterus and ovaries | The pee route is a separate system
    myth addressed: Girls pee from the vagina.
- d01-l03 [C] Hormones: The Body's Messaging System — What is behind the skin, hair, voice and chest changes
    sections: The command chain: brain to glands | Testosterone, oestrogen and progesterone | Skin, hair and voice | Breast and chest development
    myth addressed: Testosterone is only in boys and oestrogen is only in girls.
- d01-l04 [C,D] Sperm, Eggs and How a Pregnancy Begins — Ovulation, menstruation, fertilisation and implantation in order
    sections: Sperm: made daily from puberty onwards | Eggs and ovulation | Menstruation: the cycle resets | Fertilisation and pregnancy
    myth addressed: Ovulation always happens on day 14, so all the other days are safe.
- d01-l05 [D,E] The Parts Textbooks Skip — Clitoris, hymen, cervix, foreskin and prostate, without the rumours
    sections: The clitoris: mostly internal | The hymen: what it is and is not | Vagina and cervix | Foreskin, erections and the prostate
    myth addressed: Bleeding on the wedding night proves a woman is a virgin.
- d01-l06 [C,D,E] Normal Is a Range — Body diversity, intersex variations, body image and when to see a doctor
    sections: Variation is the rule | Intersex variations | Body image: who set the standard? | When to see a doctor
    myth addressed: If my body does not look like the ones online, something is wrong with it.
FAQs:
- d01-f01 [A] What are private parts?
- d01-f02 [A] Is it bad to say penis or vulva?

- d01-f04 [B,C] There is white or clear stuff in my underwear. Is something wrong with me?
- d01-f05 [B,C] One of my breasts (or testicles) is bigger than the other. Is that normal?
- d01-f06 [C] I am a boy and my chest is getting puffy with a lump under the nipple. Am I turning into a girl?
- d01-f07 [C,D] Pee and semen come out of the same tube. Can they mix or come out together?

- d01-f10 [D,E] Where exactly is the clitoris, and what is it for?

- d01-m02 [B,C] (myth) The vagina and the vulva are the same thing.
- d01-m03 [C,D,E] (myth) The mother's body decides whether the baby is a boy or a girl.

## d05 — Consent & Body Autonomy  (allowed tracks: A,B,C,D,E)

Lessons:
- d05-l01 [A] My Body Belongs to Me — You are the boss of your own body
    sections: You are the boss of your body | Ask first, then listen | Private parts stay private | Unsafe secrets and who to tell

    myth addressed: A good friend never says no.

    sections: What consent actually means | Silence, freezing and 'maybe' | Pressure is not persuasion | The age-18 line in Indian law
    myth addressed: If two people are dating, they don't need to ask each other.

    sections: When one person holds the power | How manipulation works | Alcohol, drugs and impaired judgement | Photos, chats and what Indian law says
    myth addressed: If someone accepted gifts, flirted or came over to your place, they owe you a yes.

    sections: Consent is ongoing, not a one-time contract | How adults actually ask | Marriage is not consent | Alcohol, substances and capacity
    myth addressed: Asking for consent kills the mood, and long-term partners just know.

    myth addressed: What someone wore, or being out late, is what causes sexual assault.

## d18 — Life Skills & Communication  (allowed tracks: A,B,C,D,E)

Lessons:
- d18-l01 [A] My Voice Is Strong — Saying no, listening to no and asking for help
    sections: You can say no | When someone says no, we stop | Questions are good | Tell a grown-up you trust
    myth addressed: Good children always say yes to grown-ups.
- d18-l02 [B] Say It Clearly: Feelings, Fights and Awkward Talks — 'I' sentences, saying no to friends, talking to parents and teachers, and fixing a fight
    sections: The 'I' sentence | Saying no to friends | Awkward talks with parents and teachers | How to fix a fight
    myth addressed: If I tell my parents about a problem, I will only get scolded, so it is better to hide it.
- d18-l03 [C] Your Call: Decisions, Pressure and Manipulation — A method for decisions, the tricks people use to bend your no, and how to hold it
    sections: A method for decisions that matter | How manipulation works | Holding your no | Respecting someone else's no
    myth addressed: Saying no makes you rude, and a good friend or partner never refuses.
- d18-l04 [D,E] Hard Conversations: Doctors, Parents and Friends in Trouble — What to say, what to ask and what you can expect
    sections: Getting ready for a doctor | Questions you have a right to ask | Confidentiality and its limits | Parents, and a friend in trouble
    myth addressed: If I tell the doctor the whole truth about my body or habits, they will judge me or refuse to treat me.
- d18-l05 [C,D,E] Fact-Check Mode: Health Info You Can Trust — Critical thinking, spotting fake health claims and behaving responsibly online
    sections: Why wrong information spreads faster | Five checks for any health claim | Red flags of quackery | Responsible digital behaviour
    myth addressed: If a remedy is natural or herbal, it cannot harm you.
FAQs:
- d18-f01 [A] Is it bad manners to say no to a grown-up?

- d18-m01 [A,B] (myth) Good children never say no to elders.
- d18-m02 [A,B] (myth) Telling a teacher or parent about a problem is 'chugli' (tattling).
